questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An error that occurs because a measuring instrument has a zero error and so shifts every reading in the same direction is called:
questions.explanation: Systematic errors have a definite cause and direction, so they can be corrected once identified. Random errors scatter either way and are reduced by repeating the measurement.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 1: Units and Measurements

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In simple harmonic motion, the phase difference between the displacement and the velocity of the particle is:
questions.explanation: If x = A sin ωt then v = Aω cos ωt, which leads the displacement by a quarter cycle. The acceleration is π out of phase with the displacement.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: With a rise in temperature, the resistivity of a metallic conductor and that of a semiconductor respectively:
questions.explanation: In a metal the number of carriers is fixed and more collisions raise resistivity, while in a semiconductor heating frees many more carriers, so resistivity falls sharply.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An oxidising agent is a species that:
options: Loses electrons and is itself oxidised
Gains electrons and is itself reduced
questions.explanation: An oxidising agent takes electrons from something else, so it is reduced in the process. Oxygen need not be present at all, as in the oxidation of sodium by chlorine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The addition of HBr to propene in the presence of benzoyl peroxide gives mainly 1-bromopropane. This happens because the peroxide:
options: Makes the reaction follow a free radical path, so the addition is anti-Markovnikov
questions.explanation: This is the Kharasch peroxide effect, and it is seen only with HBr, because HCl has too strong a bond and HI too weak a one to sustain the radical chain.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The equimolar mixture of glucose and fructose obtained by the hydrolysis of sucrose is called:
questions.explanation: Sucrose is dextrorotatory, but the mixture formed is laevorotatory because fructose rotates light to the left more strongly than glucose does to the right, so the sign of rotation inverts.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: In a racemose inflorescence, the main axis:
options: Ends in a flower and stops growing
Continues to grow and bears flowers laterally in acropetal order
Bears a single terminal flower only
questions.explanation: The oldest flowers are therefore at the base and the youngest at the tip. In a cymose inflorescence the axis ends in a flower, so the order is basipetal.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 5: Morphology of Flowering Plants

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Enzymes speed up a biochemical reaction mainly by:
options: Raising the temperature of the cell
Lowering the activation energy barrier of the reaction
Changing the equilibrium position in favour of products
Supplying extra energy to the substrate
questions.explanation: A catalyst never alters the equilibrium constant or the overall energy change; it only offers an easier route, which is why carbonic anhydrase can process so many molecules a second.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The glomerulus together with the Bowman's capsule enclosing it is together called the:
questions.explanation: Filtration here is called ultrafiltration because the three layered barrier lets water and small solutes through but holds back blood cells and most proteins.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 16: Excretory Products and their Elimination

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Amniocentesis is a foetal diagnostic test that has had to be legally banned for one particular use because:
options: It was being misused to determine the sex of the foetus and abort female foetuses
It is too expensive to perform
questions.explanation: The test legitimately detects disorders such as Down's syndrome and haemophilia from foetal cells in the amniotic fluid, but sex determination using it is prohibited by law in India.
